newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices steady-off $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices steady-off $1 - dealers.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hogs Monday sold steady to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by packers' plans for reduced operating hours early this week, livestock dealers said.
Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs were trading down $1.00, with $57.00 paid in the country and $58.00 to $59.50 for hogs delivered to the plant, the dealers said.
Illinois hog buyers said prices were $0.50 to $1.00 lower, at $56.50 to $57.50 in the country and $58.00 at the plant.
Indiana hogs sold steady to down $0.50 early, with $56.00 in the country and $58.00 at plants.
Ohio hog prices were steady to $0.50 lower at $56.00 to $56.50 paid in the country early and $58.00 to $58.50 at plants.
Several large packers last week said they were cutting slaughter this week in attempts to improve operating margins eroded last week by higher hog prices and weak pork values.
Estimated gross hog carcass cutout values Friday were quoted down $0.43 to $0.51 per cwt, according to USDA.
Hog marketings could be limited by increased farmer concentration on harvesting as the week progresses, sources said.
